transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm... well, I guess I'm here because I just feel like everything is my fault lately. Like, if something goes wrong at work, or even just around my house... I just feel like a bad employee. A bad homeowner. Like I just deserve to lose all the things I've worked for.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, or longer?
Longer. Um... I guess it's been about two years and a month now. Just... feeling this way, and not really having an interest in things anymore.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really felt energetic in a long time. I mostly just feel tired.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches of two months or more when you felt essentially back to your normal self, without these depressive symptoms?

Um... no. Not two months. Looking back, it's... it's pretty much been there almost the whole time since this started. Just the low mood, and... not really caring about things. 

I mean, there were maybe a few brief periods where I could function a little better, but... no, never two whole months of feeling normal.
During this two-year period, have you ever experienced significant changes in your appetite or weight, or had thoughts of death or suicide?

Um... I don't really know about my weight. I haven't been keeping track. My appetite is just... all over the place, I guess. I usually just skip real meals during the day. Sometimes I'll realize my clothes feel a little looser... but I mostly just live on coffee and toast. Whatever's easiest. 

And... no, no thoughts of suicide.
During these two years, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood, energy, sleep, or concentration became noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

I don't know... it's hard to tell. Like I said, it's just been pretty much the same low feeling the whole time. I don't really remember if there was a specific time it got worse. It just... all blends together.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a chronic depressed mood with anhedonia persisting continuously for over 2 years, without any 2-month symptom-free interval, and without any history of mania/hypomania (ruling out bipolar spectrum). No clear discrete major depressive episode with acute worsening was identified, and no psychotic or suicidal features. This pattern—chronic, low-grade depressive symptoms including low self-worth/guilt, anhedonia, appetite disturance, and fatigue lasting >2 years without remission—is most consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia), F34.1, rather than a recurrent or single major depressive episode.
